title: adaptive-concurrent-scoring-with-token-quota-safeguards
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: The reranking endpoint has growing p95/p99 latency under bursty candidate loads (large N candidates and variable token lengths). Existing single-path scoring plus coarse microbatching causes long tail stalls when token decoding or KV cache misses happen. We need an approach that improves tail latency and throughput without regressing quality for high-signal queries or increasing unit cost disproportionately.

Goals:
- Reduce p95 latency for 32-candidate reranks by at least 30% and p99 by 40% under production traffic profile.
- Maintain or improve current NDCG/Precision metrics on our in-house rerank eval set (no >1% quality regression).
- Keep token cost per query within +10% of baseline on average; avoid worst-case cost blowups.
- Provide gradual rollout via feature flag and telemetry to validate real traffic behavior.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Dual-path scoring pipeline: a fast sketch scorer (low-cost distilled model or lightweight heuristic using embeddings) produces initial ordering and early exits for obvious cases; a high-quality scorer runs in parallel for top-K candidates with a timeboxed budget.
2) Token-Quota Shepherd: allocate a per-request token budget derived from route SLAs and candidate count. The shepherd enforces soft and hard caps: soft cap triggers opportunistic yield and early-exit heuristics; hard cap cancels remaining high-cost scorer work and falls back to the sketch result.
3) Adaptive micro-concurrency: instead of fixed microbatch sizes, create short-lived micro-lanes that adapt based on observed sequence length distribution and current GPU queue depth. This reduces head-of-line blocking from a few long requests.
4) KV-prefetch advisory: when the sketch scorer indicates a high probability of re-eval, prefetch KV entries for top candidates opportunistically to reduce miss penalty. Prefetch is bounded by a per-worker budget.
5) Deadline-aware scheduling: implement per-request deadlines with graceful degradation (trim context, reduce generation tokens, or switch to quantized/fast kernel) when approaching soft deadline thresholds.

Acceptance criteria (observable):
- Performance: p95(32 candidates) decreases by >=30% in canary traffic; p99 decreases by >=40% across representative regions.
- Quality: rerank eval NDCG@10 change within +/-1% vs baseline; manual spot checks on critical queries show no regressions.
- Cost: average token consumption per request increases by <10% across canary traffic; worst-case cost capped by hard token budget.
- Stability: no increase in error rate or OOMs on canary nodes for 48h under 2x baseline load.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: Unit tests, integration tests, perf harness simulation. Internal perf run vs synthetic candidate distributions.
- Phase 1: Internal canary (10% traffic, non-critical routes). Monitor latency, quality metrics, GPU utilization, and cost.
- Phase 2: Region canaries + customer beta for select accounts with agreed SLOs.
- Phase 3: Global rollout with automatic fallback to current rerank path if error/latency regressions detected.

Metrics to capture:
- Per-request token budget consumed, breakdown fast-scorer vs high-quality scorer tokens.
- P50/P95/P99 latencies for each scoring path and end-to-end rerank.
- Frequency of soft-cap triggers and hard-cap fallbacks.
- KV-prefetch hit/miss ratio and prefetch overhead.
- Quality metrics per-run vs eval set (NDCG, MRR).
technical_notes: Sketch scorer candidate: small transformer (distilled) or embedding cosine quick-rank; must be <10ms median on GPU or CPU fallback.
Token-Quota calculation: baseBudget = basePerCandidate * N + lengthPenalty * avg_sequence_length; softCap = 0.8*baseBudget; hardCap = 1.2*baseBudget.
Micro-lane scheduler: implement lanes keyed by (route, tenant, priority) with dynamic window sizing; use token-accounting to decide yield points.
KV prefetch: advisory API from sketch scorer to serving runtime; prefetch limited to top-M candidates; prefetch budget tracked per worker with LRU eviction for aggressive memory control.
Instrumentation: add tracing spans for sketch vs high-quality scorer, token budget lifecycle, prefetch ops, and deadline-trigger events. Hook to existing Grafana dashboards: /d/rerank-latency.
Fallback: when hardCap hit, return sketch scorer ordering with a flag in response metadata; increment 'rerank.fallback.hardcap' metric.
Testing: add rerank-specific load profiles in the perf harness (candidate distributions: 8/16/32/64 and token-length mixes 16/64/256).
comments: 2026-02-28 - Priya Kapoor: Created ticket after oncall postmortem showed long tail on rerank endpoint for large candidate sets. Linked perf graphs and incident notes: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/rerank-incidents

2026-03-02 - Liam O'Neill: Spike complete. Measured a 22% p95 improvement using sketch+timebox in synthetic harness (32 candidates). Noted some regressions on queries with long contexts due to prefetch contention.

2026-03-04 - Design review (internal): Decided to prefer a small distilled sketch model instead of heuristic-only approach to keep quality consistent across edge cases. Action: DES-221 to prototype embedding UI indicators.
2026-03-06 - Engineering update: Implemented token-quota shepherd prototype and per-request tracing. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/pull/4893 (WIP).

2026-03-10 - Load test: 48h run at 2x baseline showed p95 down 34% and p99 down 41% on canary cluster; KV-prefetch caused ~3% memory overhead but improved hit ratio to 78%. Observed 7% average token increase. Preparing rollout checklist.

2026-03-11 - PM review (Ava Chen): Approved canary rollout. Ensure customer-facing metadata includes fallback flag and guidance for SDKs. Follow-up to add console dashboard for per-route fallback rate.
